leaders.priorTitle: Senior administrator (rose through the ranks; provost/senior vice president)
leaders.notes: Seventh president; joined Hofstra as an admissions officer in 1957 and rose through the ranks over a 25-year presidency. Included here as the leader in office in 1996 to anchor the chain. Died in 2016.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean of the School of Law
leaders.notes: Eighth president; named Dec 20, 2000 and served July 2001 to July 31, 2021 after more than a decade as dean of Hofstra Law School. Oversaw the 2008 and 2012 presidential debates hosted at Hofstra.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Ninth president and first woman to lead Hofstra; took office August 1, 2021, coming from UIC where she was provost and vice chancellor for academic affairs.

university: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
unit: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai

leaders.nextRole: Founding Dean Emeritus (later served as interim dean 2001-2002)
leaders.notes: Dean of Mount Sinai School of Medicine 1985-1997; included as the leader in office in 1996 to anchor the chain. The medical school's dean leads the school, distinct from the President/CEO of the affiliated Mount Sinai Health System. Died in 2025.

leaders.nextRole: Dean of the Perelman School of Medicine and EVP for the Health System
leaders.notes: Dean of Mount Sinai School of Medicine 1997-2001; left in September 2001 to become dean of Penn's medical school and EVP of the University of Pennsylvania Health System.

leaders.priorInstitution: Mount Sinai School of Medicine (same institution)
leaders.notes: Returned to serve as interim dean from August 2001 to December 2002 during the transition between Rubenstein and Davis.

leaders.priorInstitution: Mount Sinai School of Medicine (same institution)
leaders.nextRole: President and CEO (a role he held concurrently from 2003) of the Mount Sinai health enterprise
leaders.notes: Dean 2003-2007; simultaneously appointed President and CEO of Mount Sinai Medical Center in 2003, later CEO of the merged Mount Sinai Health System until 2023. Handed the deanship to Charney to focus on the CEO role.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean for Academic and Scientific Affairs (previously Dean for Research)
leaders.priorInstitution: Mount Sinai School of Medicine (same institution)
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
leaders.notes: Anne and Joel Ehrenkranz Dean 2007 to June 30, 2025, one of the longest-serving U.S. medical school deans (18 years). Had joined Mount Sinai in 2004 from Yale/NIMH before rising to the deanship.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean for Academic Affairs and Chief Scientific Officer of the Mount Sinai Health System
leaders.priorInstitution: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai (same institution)
leaders.notes: Named Anne and Joel Ehrenkranz Dean; served as interim dean beginning July 1, 2025 and was made permanent dean (announced October 27, 2025). Founding director of The Friedman Brain Institute (2008-2025) and previously Dean for Academic Affairs and Chief Scientific Officer at Mount Sinai.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean of Chicago-Kent College of Law
leaders.notes: President June 1, 1990 to August 1, 2007; one of the longest tenures in the university's history. Included as the leader in office in 1996 to anchor the chain. Had been dean of IIT's Chicago-Kent College of Law from 1974.

leaders.nextRole: Distinguished Professor of Chemical Engineering (later President of the National Academy of Engineering, 2019)
leaders.notes: President 2007-2015; came from Case Western Reserve where he was provost, and earlier was dean of engineering at Carnegie Mellon. Elected President of the National Academy of Engineering in 2019.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Senior Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Ninth president 2015-2021; a metallurgist who had been IIT's provost (2008-2015) and earlier dean of engineering at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute. Announced retirement December 2020.

leaders.priorTitle: Dunton Family Dean of the D'Amore-McKim School of Business
leaders.notes: Tenth president; took office August 2021 from Northeastern's D'Amore-McKim School of Business, where he was dean from 2017. Earlier spent eight years at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign's Gies College of Business.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean of the School of Medicine
leaders.notes: First female president of Loma Linda University, serving 1991-2008; had been the first female dean of the School of Medicine (1986-1991) and concurrently president of Loma Linda University Medical Center. Included as the leader in office in 1996 to anchor the chain.

leaders.priorTitle: Chancellor and CEO (title changed to President)
leaders.notes: Appointed president February 24, 2008, effective March 24, 2008; leads Loma Linda University Health (the Seventh-day Adventist university plus its medical center/hospitals). Served the institution since 1972, including as dean of the School of Public Health. ACTIVE SEARCH: announced retirement effective end of June 2026, and the LLUH Board of Trustees is convening a presidential search committee.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President and University Secretary (executive assistant to the president)
leaders.notes: Ninth and longest-serving LIU president, 1985-2013 (about 27 years); a historian, he came from Brandeis where he was a vice president and university secretary, and earlier taught at the University of Michigan. Included as the leader in office in 1996 to anchor the chain.

Tenth president and first woman to lead LIU; took office July 2013 from the presidency of Mercy College, and earlier was Vice Chancellor and CFO of the State University of New York (SUNY) system. Still president as of 2026.
